brightmoon-mountains-and-waters-painting.definition: A Pure Yang treasure used for the Immortal Fortunes Assembly trials; it contains a vast landscape where participants compete for token talismans.

lu-dongbin.definition: The leader of the Eight Immortals of the Upper Cave in Chinese folklore. In *Desolate Era*, he is a legendary Pure Yang True Immortal and Sword Immortal known for his passionate teaching style and his willingness to accept even mortals as disciples.

ice-phoenix-fire-phoenix.definition: Two complete Dao-based spells used by Yu Wei, representing mastery over elemental ice and fire at the Dao level.

brightmoon-landscape-world.definition: A pocket-realm painting used as the arena for the final stage of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, designed to simulate a vast wilderness where contestants hunt each other for token talismans.

messy-daoist-sanpang.definition: The Black-White College’s third-generation senior disciple, a slovenly fatty who hides his immense power behind a lazy, bone-chewing facade and wields the legendary Black Tortoise Divine Ability.

black-tortoise-divine-ability.definition: One of the top one hundred divine abilities since Pangu, originating from the Black Tortoise Grand Emperor of the Three Realms; it manifests as a turtle-snake phantom and grants terrifying physical power and defensive properties.

ten-thousand-beasts-sect.definition: A top-tier sect based in the Eastern Seas, far stronger than the Black-White College, specializing in beast-related secret arts and with hundreds of Loose Immortals and Earth Immortals.

grand-tortoise-divine-ability.definition: A supreme divine ability of the Grand Tortoise Emperor, one of the primordial overlords of the Three Realms. Its users display the distinct tortoise-shell pattern and a phantom of a tortoise-serpent.

nominal-disciple.definition: A cultivator who is listed under a major power in name only, qualified to attend lectures but rarely receiving personal guidance or core techniques.

personal-disciple.definition: A disciple personally chosen by a major power to receive full resources, secret techniques, and direct mentorship. This identity carries immense prestige and protection.

slovenly-realperson.definition: The Daoist title of Zhang Qi (Sanpang), a Wanxiang Adept of the Black-White College who secretly trained the Grand Tortoise Divine Ability and became the center of attention.

brightmoon-landscape.definition: The artificial pocket-realm and trial ground for the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, where geniuses fight for talismans and immortal fortune over many months.

taiji-grand-dao.definition: The path of the Supreme Ultimate, a Grand Dao followed by the Slovenly Realperson, focusing on balance and the interplay of Yin and Yang forces.

mingyue-water-mountain-diagram.definition: A pocket-realm treasure used by the Grand Xia to host the first major trial of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly. It contains a vast, idyllic landscape where participants hunt each other for faith-tokens, with the top 80 token holders advancing.

faith-token.definition: A token of qualification obtained by defeating or killing other participants inside the Mingyue Water-Mountain Diagram. The number of tokens a participant holds determines their rank for the first trial.

xiamang-zishan.definition: The top-ranked genius of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, a descendant of the Grand Xia imperial clan. He is a master of the Crimsonbright Diagram and possesses numerous powerful imperial divine abilities, making him a terrifying opponent.

cangwu-jiu.definition: The second-ranked genius of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, hailing from the prestigious Cangwu clan. He is a meticulous strategist and a deadly combatant, known for his keen observation and ability to recognize any threat instantly.

netherworld-poison-vulture-secret-art.definition: A signature secret art of Cangwu Vulture. It uses a formation of magic treasures to manifest a massive, spectral vulture. The caster hides within the vulture, using it for both offense and defense before bursting out for a close-range kill.

rahu-godneedles.definition: A nod to the celestial demon Rahu from Buddhist/Hindu myth. These spiritual needles are a classic Xianxia weapon. Yu Wei uses a set of 72 needles—a number resonating with the 72 Earthly Fiends in Daoist numerology—to form powerful elemental projections.

qianheaven-galewind-qian-tian-ling-feng.definition: A high-level wind-based technique used by Cangwu Vulture to trap his targets. It manifests as a massive, inescapable cyclone.

heaven-earth-myriad-pound-staff.definition: Xiamang Zishan's self-created staff art. The chapter emphasizes that his fourth form is exceptionally powerful because it fuses the power of four complete Daos into a single strike.

dao-fusion.definition: A key concept in high-level Xianxia combat. A cultivator doesn't just use a single Dao; they merge the insights of multiple Daos into a single technique, creating an effect that is exponentially more powerful than the sum of its parts.

past-life-awakening.definition: An extremely rare event where intense emotional or physical stress forces a reincarnated immortal’s sealed past-life memories to resurface.

grand-dao-of-taiji.definition: The supreme Dao of the 'Supreme Ultimate,' the ontological principle of Yin-Yang duality and unity.

luoshen-needles.definition: A set of seventy-two flying needles, a human-ranked treasure set used by Yu Wei.

brightmoon-painting.definition: A pocket dimension treasure used for the trials of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly.

grand-daoist-golden-immortal-daofather.definition: A supreme existence who has mastered a Heavenly Dao and acts as a hegemon within the Three Realms, wielding reality-altering power.

empyrean-god.definition: The Fiendgod equivalent of a Pure Yang True Immortal; a being of immense power achieved after passing the Heavenly Tribulation on the Proud Fiendgods path.

chaos-true-god.definition: The pinnacle of Fiendgod Body Refining, representing an ancient entity born from the primordial chaos, whose physical body is nigh-indestructible and whose status rivals that of a Daofather.

daofather.definition: In the Desolate Era universe, a Daofather is a supreme being of the Three Realms, the pinnacle of Ki Refining (Ancestral Immortal) who has mastered a Heavenly Dao. They are the true rulers of reality, superior even to Celestial Immortals and Pure Yang True Immortals.

ninefate-recluse.definition: A mysterious dirty girl who has comprehended five complete Daos. Xiamang Qi considers her unbeatable; she is a potential first-place contender in the Immortal Fortunes Assembly.

blackstone-recluse.definition: A barefoot, dark-skinned youth and a formation grandmaster. His Fuxi Staff Formation once scared off Xiamang Zishan and Cangwu Jiu, making him a top threat in the tournament.

landscape-of-the-brightmoon-world.definition: The pocket world used for the final trial of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, where candidates hunt each other for talismans.

ten-thousand-venoms-stinger.definition: A divine ability that refines hundreds of rare poisons into the user's palm, turning any touch into a lethal injection that bypasses physical defenses and corrupts the victim's Ki circulation.

sword-light-silken-strands.definition: The pinnacle of sword mastery in Xianxia, where a sword immortal compresses their blade's power into an impossibly thin, infinitely sharp filament, capable of cutting through magic treasures and Fiendgod bodies alike.

brightmoon-scenery.definition: The mortal-world trial zone of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, a sealed arena where contestants must gather talismans, battle for survival, and prove their mettle over the course of a real-time year.

moon-and-landscape-painting.definition: A magic treasure used during the Immortal Fortunes Assembly to create a pocket realm where Wanxiang Adepts compete for talismans.

yan-king.definition: A powerful noble of the Grand Xia Dynasty and the grandfather of Yuchi Xiyue (Xiyue Commandery Princess).

grand-freedom-and-grand-ease.definition: A state of ultimate transcendence in Daoist philosophy, achieved by having absolute power and control over one's destiny, free from all worldly and karmic constraints.

daofather-crimsonbright.definition: One of the supreme Daofathers of the Three Realms and the master of the Grand Xia Emperor. The Daofather personally oversees the selection of top talents from the Immortal Fortunes Assembly for his Crimsonbright lineage.

immortal-ranked-magic-treasure.definition: A weapon or artifact imbued with the power of an Immortal, vastly superior to mortal or Earth-ranked treasures. Only a handful exist in most commanderies, making the Emperor's offer of forty-eight a staggering show of wealth.

slovenly-trulord.definition: A slovenly, fat youth from the Black-White College. He is secretly a true disciple of Lord Xuanwu, a major power of the Three Realms, making him the pre-selected favorite of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly.

lord-xuanwu.definition: A Chaos True God and master of the Northern Seas, alluded to as a peer of Daofather Crimsonbright. He represents the pinnacle of Fiendgod Body Refining in the Three Realms.

dao-of-the-saber.definition: One of the exalted Grand Daos, celebrated for its fierce, domineering offense. A cultivator who fully comprehends it is called a Saber Immortal (or Saber Maniac) and can rival Sword Immortals in combat.

daonu.definition: Literally “Blade Servant” or “Saber Slave.” A cultivator’s self-chosen Daoist title signifying total devotion to the Saber Dao, willing to be its servant.

xia-emperor.definition: The ruler of the Grand Xia Dynasty, a figure of immense power who personally oversees the Immortal Fortunes Assembly.

ten-million-jin-of-primordial-liquid.displayTitle: Ten million jin of Primordial Liquid
surfaces: Ten million jin of Primordial Liquid
ten-million-jin-of-primordial-liquid.definition: An astronomical sum of cultivation resources. This amount of pure energy is enough to push a cultivator through multiple major stages, making it a reward befitting the utmost geniuses of the empire.

dao-of-time.definition: One of the most profound and difficult Heavenly Daos to comprehend. Even a slight mastery, like altering the flow of time for a small group, is a display of immense power and understanding.

brightmoon-waterfall-diagram.definition: A high-level magic treasure capable of creating an independent world. The Xia Emperor uses his power to alter the time flow *within* this world, giving the finalists a precious cultivation opportunity.

elder-wufeng.definition: A Loose Immortal of the Black-White College, known for his slovenly appearance and drunken demeanor, but fiercely proud of his sect.

ninefate-trulyear.definition: A dirty, disheveled-looking young girl who is actually one of the most terrifying cultivators in the top twelve, wielding the Grand Dao of Life and Death.

slovenly-trulyear.definition: The Black-White College’s top genius, a disciple of the Black Tortoise Emperor, who combines Taiji-level defense with sudden, lethal counter-strikes.

grand-dao-of-life-and-death.displayTitle: Grand Dao of Life and Death
surfaces: Grand Dao of Life and Death
grand-dao-of-life-and-death.definition: An extremely profound and powerful Grand Dao governing the transition between life and death. It grants both potent regenerative abilities and lethal attack power, making it harder to master than the Dao of the Sword.

stacking-waves.definition: A profoundly mysterious combat technique derived from the Lord Darkmarsh Divine Ability. It allows the user to endlessly stack defensive and offensive power in waves, making each subsequent attack stronger than the last until the opponent is overwhelmed.

lord-darkmarsh.definition: A supreme Daofather of the Three Realms, the master of the Slovenly True Immortal. His divine ability is the source of the "Stacking Waves" technique.

great-xia-emperor.definition: The Celestial Thearch of the Grand Xia Dynasty, a Pure Yang True Immortal who rules over countless worlds and presides over this Immortal Fortunes Assembly.

slacker-daoist.definition: A seemingly simple but immensely powerful Wanxiang Adept; already a disciple of the Black Tortoise Grand Emperor.

mu-chuan.definition: A deceptively humble genius who has been hiding his mastery of two Grand Daos (Verdant Wood and Source Water) for three hundred years.

grand-dao-of-verdant-wood.definition: A Grand Dao governing the properties of wood, growth, and life force; combined with Source Water, it becomes a devastatingly fluid defense.

grand-dao-of-source-water.definition: A Grand Dao governing the properties of water, flow, and adaptability; complements Verdant Wood in Mu Chuan's dual-Dao fighting style.

surging-waves-secret-art.definition: A technique that stacks power with each successive wave-like attack, but has a critical threshold beyond which it collapses uncontrollably.

black-tortoise-grand-emperor.definition: A Chaos True God and supreme divine beast, master of the Black Tortoise Grand Divine Ability, and the Slovenly Daoist’s hidden mentor.

the-black-white-college.definition: A premier immortal sect in Anchan Commandery, known for its elite teachings and powerful disciples like the Slovenly Daoist.

cangwu-clan.definition: A powerful ancient clan in the Grand Xia Dynasty, known for producing swift, fierce cultivators like Cangwu Crane.

sealed-formation.definition: The enclosed arena where the final battles of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly take place, binding contestants within a controlled space.

heavenly-transformation-fatiandi.definition: A divine ability that allows a cultivator to grow to massive size, embodying the scale of heaven and earth; not mere gigantification, but a sacred ontological shift.

grand-dao-of-thunder-and-lightning.displayTitle: Grand Dao of Thunder and Lightning
surfaces: Grand Dao of Thunder and Lightning
grand-dao-of-thunder-and-lightning.definition: A powerful Grand Dao focused on explosive, overwhelming force and speed; the path chosen by Xiamang Zishan.

taiji-diagram.definition: A symbol in Daoist cosmology representing the Supreme Ultimate, the origin of Yin and Yang. In Xianxia, a Taiji Diagram hovering over a character is a visual sign of supreme cosmic authority, often marking a Daofather or a being of ultimate Dao enlightenment.

floodcover-sage.definition: A Divine God (天神), one of the highest Fiendgod Body Refiners in the Three Realms. He is known for his overbearing, destructive personality and his terrifying combat power. His arrival is a major political event.

water-mirror-art.definition: A technique used to record and project visual scenes, equivalent to a magical video recording. The Xia Emperor uses it to send battle footage to Daofather Crimsonbright for evaluation.

fuhai-god-fuhai.definition: A fierce Empyrean God and Pure Yang True Immortal, a disciple of the Dark North Emperor, known for his violent temper and for once smashing the Heavenly Court.

dark-north-emperor-xuanwu-dadi.definition: A supreme Daofather-level power in the Three Realms, creator of the Dark North Grand Divine Ability, and the hidden master of the Slovenly Daoist, Zhang Qi.

grand-divine-ability.definition: A top-tier, quasi-unique cultivation technique created by a Daofather or True God, which can only be learned through direct inheritance or permission.

qi-deviation.definition: A catastrophic state of spiritual backlash in Xianxia cultivation. When a cultivator's mental state is shattered (by shock, grief, or rage), their internal energy becomes chaotic, often leading to death or transformation into a mindless demon.

xuanwu-the-grand-emperor.definition: A great power of the Three Realms, often associated with the Black Tortoise, one of the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations. He is a master of water and defensive mysteries.

fuhai-god.definition: The Empyrean God and Pure Yang True Immortal who took the Ragged Daoist as his junior apprentice-brother; depicted as fierce, crude, and deeply affectionate towards his new junior.

celestial-heaven-hall.definition: The grand main hall of the Xia Emperor's court, where the highest powers of the realm gather.

eight-immortals.definition: A group of legendary Daoist immortals in Chinese mythology, each representing a different aspect of life and society. Lu Dongbin is their leader. In this novel, they are reimagined as top-tier True Immortals of the Three Realms.

evergreen-sword-immortal.definition: A Pure Yang True Immortal and a fiercely independent disciple of Daofather Crimsonbright. He lives as a simple farmer in a minor world temple, embodying the Xianxia philosophy that only one’s own power is reliable.

crimsonbright-lineage.definition: The faction of cultivators under Daofather Crimsonbright. The top three of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly are destined for this lineage, making it the most powerful patronage network in the Grand Xia world.

top-twelve.definition: The final group of cultivators in the Immortal Fortunes Assembly, who receive a significant reward of Primordial Liquid and a chance to compete for the top three spots.

patriarch-subhuti.definition: A supreme True God born from primordial chaos and master of the Grand Dao of Spacetime in Desolate Era. He is the secretive and powerful mentor of Ji Ning, ruling over Mount Innerheart.

fiendgod-daofather.definition: A Daofather who specializes in the Fiendgod Body Refining path, making them supremely powerful in physical combat.

pure-yang-true-sword-immortal.definition: A Pure Yang True Immortal whose Grand Dao is the Dao of the Sword, making them masters of lethal, supreme offense.

eternal-sword-immortal-of-changqing.definition: The most powerful Sword Immortal under Daofather Crimsonbright's lineage in the Grand Xia Dynasty.

tristar-crescent-abode.definition: The secret cave-dwelling of Patriarch Subhuti in the Three Realms. Its name is a visual riddle: a slanted crescent and three stars form the Chinese character for “heart” (心), implying it can only be found with the heart.

celestial-immortal-evergreen.definition: A Pure Yang True Immortal and Sword Immortal of the Three Realms, junior apprentice-brother to the Grand Xia Emperor. He is known for being a recluse and was meant to take Ji Ning as a disciple.

senior-apprentice-brother-woodcutter.definition: The first and most powerful disciple of Patriarch Subhuti. He appears as a simple mortal but has lived since the Primordial Era and has never left the cave-world, embodying the concept of a ‘Hidden Immortal.’

cave-fortress-world.definition: A pocket dimension created by a major power, complete with its own natural laws and even its own cycle of reincarnation, making it fully independent from the main Three Realms.

iron-law.definition: In a Xianxia setting, an absolute rule backed by overwhelming power. On Mount Innerheart, this means instant soul annihilation for anyone who dares to fight.

starseizing-manor.definition: The true name of the aquatic palace, a legendary dwelling and inheritance left by Daoist Threelives.

dream-of-the-three-realms.definition: A supreme divine ability unique to Subhuti and Jidian that allows the user to send incarnations across all Three Realms while sleeping, perceiving everything simultaneously.

great-calamity.definition: The greatest disaster since Pangu split Heaven and Earth, which shattered the Primordial World and killed countless powerful beings.

dao-of-yin-and-yang.definition: A foundational concept in Chinese philosophy, representing the balance of complementary forces such as steadiness and sharpness.

dream-of-a-thousand-years.definition: A supreme teaching technique that allows a master to transmit a vast, experiential understanding of a Dao into a disciple's soul in a compressed dream-state, making centuries of insight feel like a single nap.

beiming-sutra.definition: A Water-element Ki Refining technique created by Daofather Xiaoyao, capable of allowing cultivation to the peak of the Three Realms' power hierarchy.

mount-innerheart.definition: The mystical mountain where Patriarch Subhuti resides and teaches his disciples. It is a sanctuary and training ground within the Tristar Crescent Major World.

congenital-spirit-treasure.definition: A legendary treasure born from Heaven and Earth after Pangu's creation, capable of taking human form and possessing innate spiritual intelligence.

divine-immortal-palace.definition: An open nine-tiered repository on Mount Innerheart containing countless techniques, formations, and secret arts accessible to all living creatures on the mountain.

three-realms-palace.definition: The most secret location on Mount Innerheart, a pavilion containing nineteen supreme divine abilities, secret arts, and formation techniques gathered by Patriarch Subhuti. Only the most talented disciples ever gain entry.

return-to-void.definition: The sixth major realm of Fiendgod Body Refining, a stage where the cultivator's body approaches the level of primordial gods.

divine-palace-of-immortals.definition: The lower library and trial ground of Mount Innerheart, containing countless techniques from the primordial era to the present, accessible only through designated service or combat trials.

silvermoon-brother.definition: The white-robed steward of the Divine Palace of Immortals and an elder disciple of Patriarch Subhuti who guides Ji Ning through the Palace’s rules.

path-of-service-trials-of-service.definition: A method of learning techniques by performing manual labor chores of increasing scope and duration, from sweeping a path to a thousand years of gate-keeping.

path-of-combat-trials-of-combat.definition: A method of learning techniques by defeating specially-created puppets that test pure Dao comprehension, forbidding the use of divine abilities or formations.

grand-dao-of-space.definition: One of the exalted Grand Daos, governing the fundamental structure of spatial dimensions. Full comprehension unlocks Greater Teleportation.

immortal-palace.definition: The main library and training hall of Mount Innerheart, divided into nine floors. Each floor contains higher-tier techniques and more difficult puppet trials.

puppet-trial.definition: A combat challenge against an ancient puppet whose tactics evolve with each defeat. The trial forces pure technique and Dao comprehension, as divine abilities are banned.

xiaoqing.definition: Ji Ning’s personal spirit-beast, a Skygreen Serpent with innate talent for the Dao of Space. She was a powerful demon at Xiantian level and has grown significantly through cultivation.

sword-tour-of-the-three-realms.displayTitle: Sword Tour of the Three Realms
surfaces: Sword Tour of the Three Realms
sword-tour-of-the-three-realms.definition: The ninth and most powerful stance of the *Three-Foot Sword*. It manifests a black dragon phantom representing wild, unrestrained power.

comparable-to-a-celestial-immortal.definition: A popular saying in the Xianxia world that means a cultivator's combat power is roughly on par with the *weakest* of Celestial Immortals, not the average or strongest.

returning-to-vacuity.definition: The Fiendgod Body Refining stage equivalent to the Ki Refining Earth Immortal stage; a Fiendgod body refiner at this level possesses godlike regenerative powers.

void-level.definition: The sixth major realm for Fiendgod Body Refiners, roughly equivalent to the Primal Daoist realm for Ki Refiners.

plowshares-sword-formation.definition: A complete set of Immortal-ranked top-grade flying swords and a matching sword art, granting Ji Ning's second truebody devastating long-range power.

triple-sealing-immortal-circlet.definition: A high-grade Immortal-ranked treasure that traps or captures enemies within its own spatial dimension.

daofather-plowshares.definition: The creator of the Plowshares sword art, a major power of the Three Realms who comprehended a Grand Dao.

immortals-palace.definition: The central repository of Dao techniques within the Tristar Crescent Abode on Mount Innerheart.

sword-roaming-the-three-realms.definition: Ji Ning’s signature offensive technique, refined over decades on Mount Innerheart, which manifests two black dragon-like sword-lights that attack in a coordinated, winding manner.

silvermoon.definition: A senior personal disciple of Patriarch Subhuti, known for his feathered fan and demeanor of confident ease; he serves as Ji Ning’s primary guide and commentator during the puppet trial.

dao-of-ink-and-wash.definition: A complete Dao comprehended overnight by the Ninth Apprentice, a painting child who had never cultivated before; a testament to the Patriarch’s ability to recognize latent talent.

jidian-senior-brother-jidian.definition: Subhuti’s second disciple, a gaunt old man who sleeps constantly but roams the Three Realms via the Dream of the Three Realms. Accumulator of boundless karmic merit and legendary figure in countless minor worlds.

houyi-archery-art.definition: A peerless divine ability ranked among the top ten since Pangu created the world. Created by the ancient god Houyi, it is the ultimate archery art of the Three Realms, capable of slaying True Gods, but with immense heartforce and equipment demands.

plow-heaven.definition: A sword-art manual written by the Daofather Plowheart, obtained by Ji Ning from the Immortal Palace’s ninth floor.

nine-heavens-mysterious-art.definition: The final manual glimpsed in this chapter; a high-tier cultivation technique whose nature is not yet revealed.

eight-nine-arcane-art.definition: The supreme divine ability beneath the True God level. It requires a Primal-level Fiendgod body to begin training and consumes enormous treasure resources to advance. Each of its nine cycles makes the body as durable as a higher-grade magic treasure, providing indestructibility without consuming divine power.

diamond-indestructible.definition: A state where the body becomes as tough as a magic treasure, so strong that even Pure Yang or Primordial treasures only produce sparks upon striking it.

primordial-treasure.definition: A treasure born from Heaven and Earth; graded as low, mid, high, and top. Comparable to the utmost limits of a Pure Yang treasure.

jidian.definition: The second senior apprentice-brother of Ji Ning, a mad monk who warns him against greed and reminds him to specialize.

houyi-archery.definition: One of the top-ten divine abilities in the Three Realms. Based on the legendary archer Houyi's techniques, it allows a cultivator to shoot a lethal arrow from a distance of a hundred thousand li or more.

crescent-major-world.definition: The major world created by Patriarch Subhuti, containing fragments of the shattered primordial Pangu’s World; a vast, hidden treasure ground for the Patriarch’s disciples.

evil-dragon-river.definition: A legendary cursed river in the Star Continent; within 1,000 li, flight and Five Elements escape techniques are suppressed. A classic Xianxia 'forbidden zone' trope that forces all combatants to fight on the ground.

star-continent.definition: One of three continents in the Crescent Major World, known for its chaotic and lawless nature with countless demon kings, tribes, and fallen kingdoms.

firewing-legion.definition: The personal elite guard of the Firewing Demon King. Even its weakest members are at the Wanxiang Adept level, and they are known for hunting down the remnants of the fallen Qi Kingdom.

qi-xiaoyu.definition: A maidservant and secret disciple of the fallen Qi Kingdom’s imperial clan. She is the target of Ji Ning’s interest due to her immense karmic merit.

shi-feng.definition: The false name used by the eldest prince of the Qi Kingdom. He is a Wanxiang Adept and the leader of the small group of fleeing survivors.

firewing-guards.definition: An elite demonic military squad wearing Dao-Soldier armor that allows them to link into a massive Firewing Insect formation; each squad contains a Primal-level great demon and eleven Wanxiang-level great demons.

firewing-guard.definition: Elite demonic guards of the Firewing Demon King, known for forming powerful Dao-soldier formations like the Firewing Centipede.

twelve-fiend-kings-of-the-eastern-stream.definition: The twelve supreme demon lords ruling the Eastern Stream region of the Star Continent; each commands vast territories and legions of demonic subordinates.

firewing-toxin.definition: A specially refined poison that merges with the victim’s body and soul upon contact, causing no direct harm but allowing the caster’s Firewing Insects to track the victim’s location from any distance.

eaststream-twelve-demon-kings.definition: A sworn brotherhood of twelve powerful demon kings ruling the Eaststream region of the Star Continent, each possessing vast karmic sin visible as a bloody aura.

great-sinner.definition: A being with massive karmic sin; in xianxia cultivation, such an aura often appears as a towering, ocean-like bloody light visible to divine sense.

trial-of-karmic-merit-and-sin.definition: A core Xianxia trope where a cultivator must balance recruiting a high-karma disciple (rare, already protected) and killing high-sin demons (extremely dangerous, proven survivors).

firewing-king.definition: The middle-ranked demon king responsible for the destruction of the Qi Kingdom; a Firewing Insect cultivator capable of deploying the Firewing Toxin.

golden-mane-bear-king.definition: The strongest of the twelve demon kings, reputed to have fought a Celestial Immortal to a standstill, forcing the immortal to retreat.

firewing-centipede.definition: A thousand-zhang-long monster formed by a dao-soldier formation; wings of fire and a centipede body, representing a unified fighting unit of hundreds of demon soldiers.

truesoul.definition: The deepest, most fundamental core of a being’s soul; destroying the truesoul prevents any form of reincarnation, representing absolute, irreversible death.

thousand-zhang.definition: A unit of length; one zhang is approximately 3.3 meters; a thousand-zhang is about 3.3 kilometers, used to emphasize the immense scale of the Firewing Centipede manifestation.

qi-royalty.definition: The surviving prince and princesses of the fallen Qi Kingdom, fleeing across the Evil Dragon River territory under the protection of Ji Ning.

eastflow-twelve-demon-kings.definition: A coalition of twelve of the most powerful, ruthless demon kings in the Star Continent. They are so strong that even Celestial Immortals are wary of opposing them.

firewing-demon-king.definition: The demon king killed in the previous chapter's ambush; he was the 'wing nexus' of the Flying Bear Grand Formation, without whom the formation cannot function.

qi-kingdom.definition: A former kingdom that was recently destroyed by the Firewing Demon King. Its remnants, including the royal family, are now under Ji Ning's protection.

void-stage.definition: The sixth major realm of Ki Refining in the Desolate Era system, following the Primal stage. It is a crucial step towards becoming a Celestial Immortal.

dongliu-twelve-demon-kings.definition: A legendary group of twelve great demon lords ruling the Star Continent, feared even by Celestial Immortals when they fight together as a formation.

flamewing-demon-king.definition: The third-ranked Demon King; a powerful great demon who tormented the imperial Qi clan and was killed by Ji Ning in a surprise attack.

goldfur-bear-demon-king.definition: The leader and most famous of the Dongliu Twelve; notably has the lowest karmic sin among them, marking him as an anomaly and a deeper threat.

qingya-xiaoyu.definition: Ji Ning's newly accepted disciple; broke with the imperial Qi clan and now sees her master as the only family she has left.

plow-the-heavens.definition: A Daofather-created sword-art that carves black gashes into the sky itself, treating space as a field to be plowed.

thousandbull-sword.definition: A Pure Yang-tier flying sword formerly owned by the Aquatic Palace. It contains the sealed formation diagram of the Ancient River, granting it battlefield control capabilities that rival a full Pure Yang treasure.

golden-furred-bear-demon-king.definition: The leader of the twelve demon kings, whose combat power matches a Celestial Immortal; uses a set of ninety-nine spherical Immortal-ranked treasures.

dongliu-monster-kings.definition: The collective name for the twelve powerful demon rulers of the Eastern Flow territory, each a Loose Immortal of considerable age.

golden-haired-bear-monster-king.definition: The leader of the Dongliu Monster Kings, a pragmatic and powerful demon who deliberately avoids karmic sin to survive his tribulations.

scattered-immortal.definition: A powerful immortal who failed their Heavenly Tribulation and survives in a state of decay, their power increasing with age.

trial-of-sin.definition: A specific type of trial in Xianxia where a cultivator must kill beings with heavy karmic sin to prove themselves worthy of an inheritance.

flying-bear-formation.definition: The combined formation the Dongliu Monster Kings use to amplify their collective power, which Ji Ning sabotaged by killing the Firewing Monster King first.

second-truebody.definition: A technique that allows a cultivator to create an independent secondary body, which Ji Ning uses to fight alongside his main body.

quya-mountains.definition: A dangerous, mist-shrouded mountain range in the Crescent Major World; the site of a secret treasure ground that the Qi Kingdom’s royal clan plundered for generations, built on fragments of the primordial Pangu’s World.

twelve-eastern-flow-demon-kings.definition: A group of twelve powerful demon kings in the Crescent Major World, formerly known for dominating the Eastern Flow region; eight were slain by Ji Ning, one he killed later, and the others fled or survived.

venomsting-demon-king.definition: The fourth-ranked of the Twelve Eastern Flow Demon Kings; survived the initial massacre but was later hunted down and killed by Ji Ning for his karmic sin.

qi-rufeng.definition: The prince of the Qi Kingdom, whose hesitation to share his clan’s treasure map led to Ji Ning rejecting him as a disciple.

evil-loose-immortal-patriarch.definition: A six-hundred-thousand-year-old human Loose Immortal and the strongest of an evil sect; slain by Ji Ning in a protracted battle, yielding massive killing intent for his Northsea swords.

trial-by-combat.definition: A core Xianxia trope where a cultivator's pure technique and Dao comprehension are tested against a mirror match or a restrictive environment, often banning divine abilities or formations.

karmic-merit-light.definition: A visible aura of accumulated good deeds; the taller the light, the purer the cultivator's soul and the more favored they are by the Heavenly Dao. Ji Ning’s three feet contrasts with his disciple’s three hundred zhang.

houyi-s-archery-art.definition: A top-ten divine ability in the Three Realms created by the legendary archer Houyi. It is a technique-based art of archery that has surpassed the standard 'Dao of Archery,' requiring immense comprehension to master.

seventy-two-transformations.definition: The foundational requirement for entering the Eight-Nine Arcane Art. It allows the cultivator to perfectly transform their body and aura into anything that exists in the Three Realms, from rocks and trees to powerful gods.

silvermoon-empyrean-god.definition: An Empyrean God managing the Palace of Immortals on Mount Innerheart; lent Ji Ning a hundred Immortal-ranked pills for the Eight-Nine Arcane Art, executing a shrewd social transaction that recovers his full investment.

karmic-hellfire.definition: A flame of pure cosmic judgment that burns a cultivator from the soul outward, triggered by the sin of mass slaughter. It ignores physical defenses and can kill even Immortals, serving as the universe's ultimate deterrent against genocide.

immortal-ranked-supreme-elixir.definition: A high-grade restoration pill containing energy as pure as a Celestial Immortal's own magic power. Used for rapid breakthroughs or emergency power replenishment; worth the equivalent of a high-grade Immortal-ranked treasure each.

silvermoon-archdemon.definition: The nickname for senior apprentice-brother Silvermoon, an Empyrean God known for his mercilessly shrewd dealings with fellow Mt. Innerheart disciples.

celestial-immortal-wuyai.definition: A Celestial Immortal and Mount Innerheart disciple recruited by the Golden-Furred Bear King to help conquer the thunder forbidden zone; instantly recognizes Ji Ning’s Eight-Nine Arcane Art and defers to him as an uncle-master.

tristar-crescent-realm.definition: The pocket dimension world containing Mount Innerheart, home to Patriarch Subhuti’s disciples; outsiders cannot enter without permission.

thunder-forbidden-zone.definition: A one-hundred-eighty-zhang barrier within the Quya Mountain treasure ground that unleashes lethal lightning bolts; forces that rival high-Celestial Immortal attacks appear beyond one hundred sixty zhang.

fiendgod-corpse.definition: The body of a primordial being whose soul was so integrated with its flesh that residual will and killing intent can persist for ages after death.

protocosmic-spirit-treasure.definition: The highest tier of treasure in the Desolate Era setting, born from the natural laws of the primordial chaos. Possessing one is a game-changer for any cultivator.

water-heavens.definition: A defensive sword art from the ninth level of the Divine Immortal Palace at Mount Innerheart, specializing in fluid, water-like defense.

i-eat-tomatoes-fanqie.definition: The pen name of the author of *Desolate Era*, one of the most prolific and beloved Chinese web novelists, known for his fast-paced cultivation stories and reliable update schedule.

volume-13.definition: The current story volume focusing on Ji Ning's training under his master; its conclusion signals a major turning point as the protagonist prepares to re-enter the wider cultivation world.

innate-spirit-treasure.definition: A treasure born from the primordial forces of Heaven and Earth, possessing its own spiritual nature. Unlike refined treasures, it can choose its own master and is extremely difficult to forcibly refine.

luohu-bow.definition: A top-grade innate spirit treasure forged from the corpse of the ancient terror Luohu. It is one of the ten great divine bows of the Primordial Pangu World.

houyi.definition: The legendary archer who shot down nine of the ten suns. In Desolate Era, his archery art is one of the most difficult trials in the Three Realms Palace.

primordial-pangu-world.definition: The original, primordial world from which the current Three Realms were formed after its destruction. Beings from this world, like the Xia Emperor, are considered to have deep, ancient lineages and hidden powers.

candle-dragon-eye.definition: A supreme divine ability for vision, cultivated by gathering the Nine Heavens' Aurora into the eyes. It allows a cultivator to see across vast distances, even peering through space itself.

big-senior-apprentice-brother.definition: The first and most senior disciple under a master. In Xianxia, this figure is often the quiet powerhouse, representing the peak standard of the sect's disciples.

heart-of-absolute-sincerity.definition: A Daoist concept where total, unwavering commitment to a single discipline unlocks profound power and understanding. It is considered more important than raw talent for achieving mastery.

candle-dragon-s-gaze.definition: A powerful ocular divine ability activated by Ji Ning. In mythology, the Candle Dragon (Zhulong) is a primordial god whose eyes create day and night. The ability grants him the power to see through nearly all illusions, stealth, and spatial distortions.

nine-heavens-annihilating-wind.definition: A movement-type divine ability Ji Ning has recently learned; its minor mastery allows him to ride the wind at extreme speeds, showing his rapid skill acquisition.

northsea-hall.definition: The most important hall of the rebuilt Ten Thousand Swords City, named after Ji Ning's Daoist title 'Darknorth'. Symbolizes his elevated status within the clan.

immortal-duohe-and-immortal-wusui.definition: Two demonic immortals (狐妖仙人, wolf-immortal) who serve the Ji Clan as protectors. Descendants of Celestial Immortal Wujiang.

ji-liuzhen.definition: The current Patriarch of the Ji Clan after Ji Jiuhuo's passing. Manages the clan's affairs during Ji Ning's absence.

author-s-note.definition: A direct message from a Chinese web novel author to their readers, often inserted into the chapter release schedule to explain delays, build hype, or share behind-the-scenes thoughts.

grand-narrative.definition: A term used by the author to describe the overarching, epic-scale storyline that connects all the smaller arcs, marking a significant shift in the novel's scope and complexity.

factions.definition: Organized groups or powers within the Xianxia world, each with its own leaders, goals, internal rules, and methods. Their careful definition is crucial for a complex plot.

mountain-carrying-celestial-immortal.definition: A powerful Celestial Immortal under the Beishan clan of Anchan, known for his hunched back and wooden staff; serves as the clan's top intelligence figure and diplomatic envoy.

wufeng-immortal.definition: The oldest Loose Immortal of the Black-White College, known for his slovenly appearance. Here, he delivers the critical news of the Diancai Immortal’s impending tribulation.

beishan-heihu.definition: The father of Beishan Baiwei and the former primary rival to Beishan Yin in the struggle for the Marquis title; still living in his old estate in Anchan City.

bihai-daoist.definition: Former College Lord of the Black-White College; a Primal Daoist who recently broke through to become an Earth Immortal.

pure-yang-level-technique.definition: A superior Ki Refining technique that provides an unparalleled foundation for a cultivator's Dao, far surpassing ordinary Immortal-level techniques.

blood-god-church.definition: One of the eight great powers of the Anchan Commandery, recently revealed to be far more powerful than its surface strength, capable of stalemating the ruling Northmont clan.

tuoshan-celestial-immortal.definition: A Celestial Immortal aligned with the Anchan Northmont clan, who fought the Blood God Church's leader to a standstill.

realperson.definition: A title for a Wanxiang Adept, indicating their mastery of the Dao and respectable status in the cultivation world.

northmi-peak.definition: Ji Ning's personal peak within the Black-White College, named after his Dao-title.

bloodcloud-hall.definition: A mysterious and highly effective assassination organization that appeared in the Grand Xia world thirty years prior. It swears by a Heavenly Dao Oath to protect client secrecy, making it the perfect tool for the powerful.

ancestor-mysterious-mystic.definition: A Celestial Immortal of the Shaoyin clan, willing to pay an enormous price to eliminate the rising threat of Ji Ning.

top-grade-immortal-ranked-treasure.definition: The highest grade of magic treasure below the Pure Yang level, invaluable even to Celestial Immortals for both offense and defense.

yuchi-xiyue.definition: The Xiyue Commandery Princess, Ji Ning's cousin, and the heir of the fallen Yuchi clan. She is coldly pragmatic, willing to tolerate a wealthy suitor's arrogance purely to extract resources for rebuilding her clan.

windbinding-island.definition: A minor power in the Heavenly Realm, currently allied with the Grand Xia Dynasty through a marriage pact.

feng-yunpeng.definition: An arrogant son of the Island Lord of Windbinding Island, a Earth Immortal-level cultivator who openly pursues Yuchi Xiyue.

feng-yungu.definition: A humble, inferior young man from Windbinding Island, willing to marry into Yuchi Xiyue’s clan.

fire-elephant-arrow.definition: An arrow fired from the Luohou Bow, each one equivalent in value to a low-grade Pure Yang treasure. Divine archers of the Three Realms must have specially crafted arrows that can survive being shot from legendary bows, making each arrow a disposable top-tier weapon.

young-master-yunpeng.definition: A proud noble from the Windstop Isle of the Heavenly Realm, pursuing Yuchi Xiyue. He is arrogant, wealthy, and uses his resources to flaunt status, making him a prime target for social humiliation in this chapter.

luohou-bow.definition: A supreme-grade innate spirit treasure obtained by Ji Ning from the Divine Fiend corpse in Chiya Mountain. It is a legendary bow of the Three Realms, and its arrows are Pure Yang-level artifacts.

green-willow-immortal.definition: The white-robed female immortal in charge of high-end transactions at Heavenly Treasures Mountain's headquarters, deferring to her Celestial Immortal ancestor for major deals.

portable-immortal-manor.definition: A magic treasure that can shrink to the size of a palm and expand into a full-sized living estate; considered a luxury item for powerful cultivators.

heavenly-fox.definition: A Celestial Immortal spirit-beast of the Grand Xia Emperor, founder of Heavenly Treasures Mountain, responsible for all of its operations.

face-mi-nzi.definition: A Chinese social concept representing one's reputation, status, and dignity in public; losing face is a form of social defeat that can trigger withdrawal, hostility, or strategic retreat.

mind-mazing-eighteen-illusion-formation.definition: A complex illusion-type formation that confuses and traps intruders, making them hopelessly lost. Its core is set around Serpentwing Lake.

three-great-lethal-formations.definition: A set of three legendary, exceptionally powerful defensive formations that Ji Ning plans to set up around Yan Mountain to guarantee its safety.

sealing-type-formation.definition: A formation that cannot be bypassed through cleverness or technique; it must be broken by raw, overwhelming force, requiring the strength of a True Immortal or Empyrean God.

immortal-wufeng.definition: The oldest Loose Immortal of the Black-White College, known for his slovenly appearance; he will serve as one of the Diancai Immortal’s protectors.

late-void-stage.definition: The final stage before facing the Heavenly Tribulation; Ji Ning, Uncle White, and Xiaoqing all reach this level in this chapter.

golden-lotus-primordial-soul.definition: The manifestation of a late-stage Primal soul; Ji Ning’s reaches near-maturity with a single seed at its center.

golden-lotus-primal.definition: The foundational energy core of an Earth Immortal's soul, formed after a successful Primal-to-Earth-Immortal breakthrough; burning it is a suicidal forbidden technique.

supreme-grade-immortal-ranked.definition: The highest quality tier of magic treasures in the Grand Xia realm, extremely rare and powerful.

celestial-wind.definition: A formless, unstoppable force that tests the cultivator’s Dao-heart directly by entering through the crown of the head; cannot be blocked by any physical or magical defense.

celestial-fire.definition: The final stage of the Fire Tribulation, a primordial flame that burns within the cultivator's body to temper their physical form.

five-elements-sword-intent.definition: An advanced level of sword mastery demonstrated by the Diancai Immortal, combining the power of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water.

top-grade-immortal-ranked-flying-sword.definition: The highest quality tier of magic treasure commonly found in the Grand Xia realm, vastly superior to high-grade swords. A single one is a clan heirloom; a matching set of five is a king's ransom.

three-talents-sword-formation.definition: A classic sword formation based on the Daoist concept of Heaven, Earth, and Man, used to enhance the power and stability of a group of flying swords.

five-elements-sword-formation.definition: A sword formation based on the interplay of the five fundamental elements (Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth), creating a stable and powerful defensive or offensive array.

six-nine-tribulation.definition: A Heavenly Tribulation involving 54 thunderbolts; a cultivator who overcomes this threshold is considered a legitimate, powerful Celestial Immortal, far above those who only passed a weaker tribulation.

five-elements-sword-art.definition: A profound sword technique based on the interactions of the Five Elements (Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water). Its 'Lesser' volume (first 18 stances) culminates in the 'Lesser Five Elements Annihilation' stance.

lesser-five-elements-annihilation.definition: The final, grand completion stance of the first volume of the Five Elements Sword Art. It manifests as a single, crushing Five Finger Mountain that represents the extreme of despair.

celestial-immortal-body.definition: The transcendent physical form achieved by a cultivator who successfully survives their tribulation, marking the transition from mortal to immortal life and granting freedom from natural lifespan limits.

bloodshadow-god.definition: The leader of the Blood God Church, a powerful cult in the Anchan Commandery powerful enough to contend with the local Beishan clan. His name comes from his blood-red robes and demeanor.

bloodcry-hall.definition: A terrifying and mysterious assassin organization operating within the Grand Xia Dynasty. They are known for their elite killers and their extreme caution regarding the hidden masters of their targets.

heart-tribulation.definition: The final and most dangerous stage of a Heavenly Tribulation. Unlike the elemental tribulations, the Heart Tribulation attacks the cultivator’s mind and soul, trapping them in a mental world for what feels like years or millennia until they succumb to illusion or break through to enlightenment.

returning-void-earth-immortal.definition: The last major cultivation stage before Celestial Immortal. A Returning Void cultivator is an Earth Immortal, a being who has transcended the Five Elements but must undergo the Heavenly Tribulation to achieve immortality. “Tribulation Transcending” specifically refers to the act of enduring this final test.

spatial-teleportation.definition: A method of instantaneous travel used by powerful cultivators. It bypasses physical distance but cannot be used in all locations, as it can be blocked by powerful formations or unstable space.

heart-demon-tribulation.definition: The most dangerous of the four major tribulations. It is a mental and spiritual attack that targets the deepest flaws and insecurities within a cultivator's Dao-heart, forcing them to overcome their inner demons.

dharma-king-formation.definition: A technique that allows multiple cultivators to merge their power into a single entity, greatly boosting their combat capabilities.

blood-dragon-formation.definition: The Seven Dharma Kings’ signature formation; they combine their auras into a thousand-zhang blood dragon.

bashe.definition: An ancient python-like divine beast capable of growing to thousands of zhang. It is a common transformation for high-level cultivators in combat.

li-tian-sword-formation.definition: A sword formation created by a Daofather, perfectly matched with the Li Tian series of swords. It is known for its powerful and elegant area-of-effect attacks.

pure-yang-purely-yang-treasure.definition: The highest tier of artificial magic treasure, exclusive to Celestial Immortals. The Qianqiu Sword is a “nearly Purely Yang” weapon, making it the absolute peak of the Immortal grade.

grand-teleportation-dao-seal.definition: An extraordinarily rare and precious single-use talisman that allows a user to instantly teleport across vast distances, even through spatial seals.

basilisk-formation.definition: A high-tier, twelve-man formation used by Bloodcloud Hall that projects a single, massive Basilisk construct, pooling the strength of all twelve Immortal-level cultivators. It has multiple tiers of forbidden arts.

ancient-river-formation-diagram.definition: A Pure Yang-tier formation diagram sealed within the Thousandbull Sword. When activated, it manifests the legendary ten-thousand-li Ancient River as a battlefield control zone that binds, crushes, and suppresses all enemies within its range.

primal-stage.definition: The seventh major realm of cultivation in Desolate Era. Ji Ning is currently at the late-stage of Primal in his true body (Fiendgod path), capable of wielding the Thousandbull Sword’s formation diagram.

viper-prison.definition: A powerful forbidden art conjured by 12 assassins that takes the form of a massive serpent. Its corrosive power can kill returned-void Fiendgods and Celestial Immortals, but cannot harm a body comparable to an Immortal-ranked treasure.

soulvessel-river.definition: The river of sword-light unleashed by Ji Ning's Thousandbull Sword. It can expand from ten li to ten thousand li in length and grinds against enemies with immense, sweeping power.

samsara-talisman.definition: A legendary Pure Yang treasure capable of forcibly reincarnating a target's soul and imprinting loyalty into their being, essentially 'brainwashing' them in their next life without destroying their cultivation.

forbidden-zone.definition: A restricted area within a sect's territory, often used by a conquering force for secret projects. Entry is forbidden to all but the invaders' own subordinates.

ashen-divine-fire.definition: A legendary flame that can threaten even a Celestial Immortal. In Xianxia, such fires are typically formed from the condensation of the Dao of Fire and are highly effective against Ki Refiners and fragile bodies, but useless against supreme body-refining techniques like the Eight-Nine Arcane Art.

three-tailed-thundergod-beast.definition: A rare, high-quality combat puppet powered by divine lightning. In Xianxia, such puppets are extremely valuable and often reserved for elite enforcers or sect protectors. Ji Ning shatters one with a single sword blow, showcasing the sheer quality gap.

face.definition: A Chinese social concept representing one's reputation and dignity. The general's refusal to fight is framed as a "face" calculation—the risk isn't worth the reward.

three-tailed-thunder-god-puppet.definition: A powerful puppet crafted by a Thunder God, capable of fighting at the Celestial Immortal level; its pilot, Han Da, is a cowardly but pragmatic subordinate.

ba-serpent.definition: A massive divine serpent used by the D-9 squad for close-quarters combat and spatial containment; a classic Xianxia binding beast.

nine-heavens-divine-poison-flame.definition: A chaotic, vile True Fire of mixed elemental power; cannot be nurtured within an immortal's body and is considered a dangerous, uncontrollable flame that requires a grand formation to deploy.

portable-immortal-mansion.definition: A cultivator's personal mobile dwelling and treasure; can be used to hide from attacks but leaves the cultivator vulnerable to spatial sealing or being sent to a dangerous location.

immortal-ranked-supreme-grade-treasure.definition: A top-tier treasure within the Immortal grade of magical artifacts; twenty of these are equivalent in value to two Pure Yang treasures.

golden-core.definition: In Daoist alchemy, a condensate of one’s essence, energy, and spirit; in Desolate Era, it marks the final unity of the Primal soul and Yuan power, granting true immortality and freedom from periodic tribulations.

anchan-northmont-clan.definition: The ruling marquis clan of the Anchan Commandery; they protect sects like the Black-White College in exchange for talent recruitment rights and loyalty; a Celestial Immortal in the college shifts the power balance.

greater-teleportation-dao-seal.definition: A rare, one-use talisman that allows instantaneous teleportation across the world; considered a high-value escape tool used only in desperate situations.

tribulation.definition: The heavenly ordeal a cultivator must face to break through to a higher realm. For the Celestial Immortal level, this includes the Wind, Fire, Thunder, and Heart-Demon Tribulations.

karma.definition: The universal law of cause and effect. In Xianxia, every action, friendship, and bond creates Karmic ties (因果). Severing these ties is a strategy to avoid attracting danger and living a long, isolated life.

grand-xia-world.definition: The primary setting of the early narrative; a vast major world within the Three Realms, ruled by the Xia Emperor.

basilisk-combined-formation.definition: A rare and powerful formation technique. The name suggests it imitates the fabled giant serpent, the Bashe (巴蛇), a creature from Chinese mythology capable of swallowing elephants.

cloud-of-blood-tower.definition: The foremost assassin organization in the Grand Xia World. An ancient and shadowy force, revealed to be a key pawn of the mysterious hidden hand opposing the Grand Xia Dynasty.

ancestral-celestial-fox.definition: The founder of Heavenly Treasures Mountain; a powerful figure whose personal appearance signals a matter of extreme importance and the high status of the person making the inquiry.

feigned-death.definition: A strategic philosophy where a powerful cultivator pretends to die to sever their Karmic ties and avoid being drawn into the conflicts and tribulations of the world.

seamless-gate.definition: A mysterious and incredibly powerful organization from outside the Three Realms, operating as a shadowy force that rivals the established powers like the Grand Xia.

golden-robed-emissaries.definition: Celestial Immortals who serve as the Seamless Gate’s representatives and enforcers; the pinnacle of its revealed hierarchy.

bashe-formation.definition: A formation commonly used by Bloodcloud Hall assassins, named after the mythical giant serpent Bashe.

silver-haired-man.definition: The Xia Emperor’s incarnation, who provides Ji Ning with the intelligence report on the hidden powers.

heavenly-edict-hall.definition: The main venue of the Grand Xia’s Immortal Fortunes Assembly; where over a thousand Celestial Immortals once gathered.

taiyin-true-water-sunstar-true-fire.definition: The primordial waters of the lunar star and the primordial flames of the solar star. When fused, they can weave a cocoon of energy that fundamentally reconstructs a Fiendgod Body Refiner’s physique.

fivefold-thunderlight-ark.definition: A supreme-grade Immortal-ranked ark that can match a True God’s speed and unleash the Fivefold Thunderlight, a technique on par with the Nine Heavens Divine-Poison Flame.

celestial-earth-fiendweb-formation.definition: A set of 3,600 supreme-grade Immortal-ranked flying knives that form a devastating killing formation, overwhelming enemies through sheer quantity and formation synergy.

starry-zhou-heavenly-sword-formation.definition: A set of 360 supreme-grade Immortal-ranked flying swords that manifests the ancient Starry Zhou Grand Formation, each sword striking with the force of a falling star.

yin-yang-twin-polarity-thousand-slaughte.displayTitle: Yin-Yang Twin Polarity Thousand Slaughter Formation
surfaces: Yin-Yang Twin Polarity Thousand Slaughter Formation
yin-yang-twin-polarity-thousand-slaughte.definition: A supreme-grade set of one thousand flying swords (500 Yin, 500 Yang) that can be deployed as a devastating formation, capable of annihilating everything in its path.

grand-thousand-sword-formation.definition: A powerful sword formation technique that can amplify the power of multiple flying swords into a single, devastating attack, typically manifested as a divine dragon.

grand-thousand-sigil.definition: A highly complex runic sigil imprinted onto flying swords used in the Grand Thousand Sword Formation, requiring significant time and energy to inscribe.

east-forest-sect.definition: A sect located within the East Forest Mountain Range, currently under the control of unknown powerful figures who have subjugated its members.

soul-search.definition: A secret art used to forcibly extract memories from a target’s soul. It risks permanent mental damage or death for the victim if they resist, making it a feared tool of interrogation.

forbidden-ground.definition: A highly restricted area, often protected by powerful formations and guards. In this context, it is used as a secret base and prison by the mysterious occupying force.

transformation-technique.definition: A magical art that allows a cultivator to change their form, such as turning into an animal or a different person.

divine-fiend-puppet.definition: A supremely powerful class of artificial construct, forged by puppet grandmasters using Dao matrices. The top-tier version described here can single-handedly dominate battlefields against dozens of Celestial Immortals.

immortal-ranked-flying-sword.definition: A weapon imbued with the power of an immortal’s Dao, classified as a graded treasure above Mortal, Earth, and Heaven ranks. Supreme-grade Immortal-ranked blades are among the finest weapons available to cultivators below the True God level.

true-immortal-true-god.definition: Two of the highest cultivation stages, representing the absolute peak of power in the known universe. They are the benchmark used to measure the puppet’s terrifying strength.

fiendgod-puppet.definition: A massive, thousand-meter-tall war golem, often shaped like a giant crab. In *Desolate Era*, it is the ultimate weapon of the enemy forces, crafted by hundreds of enslaved Puppetmasters. When piloted by a Celestial Immortal, it possesses power nearly unrivaled except by True Gods and Celestial Immortals.

demon-guard.definition: In the enemy’s hierarchy, a Demon Guard is a powerful Loose Immortal-level enforcer, roughly on par with the "Evil Ancestor" in combat power. They serve as the elite security force of the stronghold, ranking above the common Demon Servants and below the Celestial Immortal-level Demon Generals.

qu-huan.definition: A red-robed overseer of the enemy stronghold. He is a low-status Demon Servant who gained his authority through political maneuvering rather than combat skill, making him a hated figure among the other demon servants and a perfect target for Ji Ning's assassination.

void-fiendgod.definition: A Fiendgod Body Refining cultivator at the Void stage, possessing a powerful, near-indestructible divine body and immense strength.

pixiu.definition: A divine beast from Chinese mythology, the Pixiu is one of the nine legendary sons of the Ancestor Dragon. In Desolate Era, it is conjured as a formation by Bronze Demon Guards, transforming nine soldiers into a single powerful war-beast.

ancestor-dragon.definition: In the novel's cosmology, the first dragon born from the primordial chaos, even older than Torch Dragon. She is the mother of all dragons and gave birth to nine divine sons, including the Pixiu.

binding-type-treasure.definition: In Desolate Era, binding-type treasures (like ropes or nets) are a specific counter to forms of invulnerability such as the Eight-Nine Arcane Art. They restrict movement and prevent the use of escape talismans, representing a tactical vulnerability for otherwise indestructible cultivators.

greater-thousand-swords-formation.definition: Ji Ning’s signature sword formation, an upgraded version of the Lesser Thousand Sword Formation. At the fourth level, it synchronizes over 300 flying swords to deliver a devastating, single-strike attack.

supreme-grade-immortal-ranked-flying-swo.definition: The highest grade of Immortal-ranked treasure, representing the peak of power for such artifacts, far surpassing common or even top-grade Immortal treasures.

soul-prison-jade.definition: A legendary Xianxia material that permanently bonds with a soul placed inside it. The soul becomes one with the jade and cannot leave, suffering eternal confinement without hope for reincarnation.

pure-yang-low-grade-seals.definition: A grade of magic treasure surpassing Immortal-ranked artifacts. These are treasures used by True Immortals and True Gods, immensely powerful and rare.

dao-oath.definition: A magically binding promise sworn to the universe itself. Breaking a Dao Oath results in catastrophic karmic backlash, often causing instant death or cultivation collapse. It is a powerful tool for binding allies or enemies to a specific course of action.

nine-heavens-divine-poison-flame-furnace.definition: A grand formation that manifests as floating mountain peaks and generates a chaotic True Fire of mixed elemental power. It is a devastating siege weapon, capable of threatening even Celestial Immortals.

daofather-yinglong.definition: A supreme Daofather-level being from Chinese mythology, associated with the Yinglong (a winged dragon). In this universe, he is a major power in the Three Realms and a sworn brother of the Grand Xia Emperor.

beishan-major-world.definition: One of the many Major Worlds within a Realmverse. Unlike the unified and relatively peaceful Grand Xia World, the Beishan Major World is a chaotic battlefield, making it a dangerous posting for any cultivator.

buousi.definition: The Zifu-level general of the Forbidden Ground whom Ji Ning killed in a previous chapter; a respected figure whose defeat marks Ji Ning as a high-level threat.

fairy-wing.definition: The second-ranked puppet in the Forbidden Ground's arsenal, capable of unleashing Seven Cycle Wind-Thunder and granting a Celestial Immortal's combat power to its user.

five-elements-treasures.definition: Rare ingredients required to train the higher stages of the Starseizing Hand divine ability; a key goal in Ji Ning's current power-up arc.

skygold-crystal.definition: A rare celestial metal used in crafting high-tier magic treasures, often associated with the Metal element.

pure-yang-top-grade-magic-treasure.definition: A treasure of immense power, comparable to a mid-grade Innate spirit-treasure. It is a standard high-end asset for Pure Yang True Immortals and Heavenly Gods.

six-cycles-of-the-starseizing-hand.displayTitle: Six Cycles of the Starseizing Hand
surfaces: Six Cycles of the Starseizing Hand
six-cycles-of-the-starseizing-hand.definition: A legendary divine ability created by Daofather Threelives, ranked among the top ten in the Three Realms. It trains the hands to become as powerful as magic treasures.

ten-yama-kings.definition: In Chinese Buddhist and Daoist cosmology, the ten judges of the underworld who preside over the courts of Diyu, evaluating the sins of the dead and dictating their reincarnation.

ancestor-chixin.definition: A formidable Celestial Immortal of the Shaoyan clan, recognized as one of the strongest among their ranks, assigned to lead the assassination squad against Ji Ning.

ten-kings-of-hell.definition: In Chinese Buddhist and Daoist cosmology, the Ten Kings of Hell are the judges of the underworld who preside over the courts of Diyu, judging the dead based on their sins. In Desolate Era, there are now nearly a thousand such kings, each overseeing a minor cycle of reincarnation.

book-of-life-and-death.definition: A legendary artifact in Chinese mythology, said to be able to control the lifespan and death of all living beings. In the novel, the original one was a supremely powerful treasure perfectly attuned to the Heavenly Dao, capable of recording all karmic information.

minor-cycle-of-reincarnation.definition: A smaller, localized version of the Six Paths of Reincarnation, established by Daofather Crimsonbright after the original collapsed. It lacks the power and omniscience of the original Netherworld Kingdom’s system.

first-judge-lord-cui.definition: The chief judge of the original Netherworld Kingdom, wielding the Book of Life and Death. A key figure in Chinese folklore, he acts as a guide for souls and is a powerful ally of the protagonist in the story.

soul-based-attack.definition: A rare and insidious form of attack in Xianxia that targets a cultivator's soul or spirit directly, bypassing most physical defenses. It is a test of one's Dao-heart and soul strength, not their magical power.

ancestor-bitterwood.definition: An ancient Celestial Immortal of the Shaoyin clan, known as an anomaly for mastering powerful spell techniques instead of using magic treasures. His signature ability summons a 'forest' of devastating vines.

seven-cyclones-thunder.definition: A powerful wind-and-lightning attack unleashed by the Winged Immortal Puppet, capable of matching the strength of a Celestial Immortal.

grand-qian-sword-formation-fourth-stage.definition: Ji Ning's current ultimate offensive technique, transforming the sword-light of hundreds of flying swords into a single, devastating black dragon.

messenger-talisman.definition: A soul-bound token used by allied cultivators to signal for help in an emergency. Destroying the talisman alerts the allies to the holder's location and danger.

omniscient-earth-mirror.definition: A Pure Yang-ranked magic treasure capable of scrying on any location within a certain area, allowing its owner to spy on distant events.

divine-bell.definition: A supreme-grade Pure Yang magic treasure owned by the Shaoyin clan, implying the clan is deploying its absolute heaviest firepower to guarantee Ji Ning's death.

pure-yang-ranked-top-grade-magic-treasur.definition: A treasure of the highest tier wielded by Celestial Immortals in the Three Realms, possessing immense, world-shaking power and often serving as a clan's heirloom.

yixian-puppet.definition: A powerful, Immortal-ranked puppet known for its flight capabilities, controlled by a cultivator's divine sense. Here, it is piloted by Mu Northson.

nine-heavens-astral-wind.definition: A grand divine ability that grants the user incredible speed and agility, allowing them to move like an untouchable breeze through a battlefield.

five-finger-mountain.definition: The combined manifestation of the Five Element Sword Art’s ‘Lesser Five Elements Annihilation’. The five mountain phantoms represent the crushing weight and extinction of the five elements.

grand-unity-sealing-circle.definition: A legendary binding treasure mentioned in this chapter, used to counter the Eight-Nine Arcane Art.

redsnow.definition: An Empyrean God and former subordinate of Godking Threelives. He has been waiting in the War God Hall for eons to test the Godking's chosen successor.

pure-yang-perfection.definition: The highest tier of standard Immortal-ranked magic treasures, representing the absolute best of their class. Achieving this level is a massive qualitative leap in a cultivator's power.

red-maned-empyrean-god-hongxue.definition: An ancient Empyrean God who served under the aquatic palace's original master, left as a trial. His incarnation is incredibly powerful but has very limited divine power.

starseizing-hand-fourth-cycle.definition: The fourth stage of the legendary Starseizing Hand divine ability. At this level, a cultivator's hands become comparable to Pure Yang ultimate magic treasures in durability.

one-breath-nine-primeval-pearls.definition: A famous Pure Yang magic treasure set from the primordial Pangu's World, capable of transforming into nine independent worlds for devastating attacks.

fuxi-staff-formations.definition: Formation sets named after the legendary Fuxi, used by formation masters for rapid deployment in battle.

celestial-fox.definition: A silver-haired, high-level manager at the Heavenly Treasures Mountain, serving as a direct intermediary with the Grand Xia Emperor.

vast-nine-orbs.definition: A rare 'World-type' Pure Yang treasure set consisting of nine high-grade orbs and a single top-grade core orb, used to crush or imprison enemies.

rahu-bow.definition: A high-grade innate spirit-treasure bow, a signature weapon of the ancient Fiendgod Rahu, known for its devastating power.

ancient-imperial-clan.definition: The former ruling lineage of the unified Pangu World, a supremely powerful clan of cultivators. The Xiamang clan of the Grand Xia is a diminished branch.

million-cultivators.definition: A Xianxia trope representing the numerical might of a top-tier ancient clan. While most are low-level, their sheer numbers and layered formations make a lair nearly impossible for a normal Immortal to assault.

soul-searching.definition: An invasive interrogation technique where a cultivator forcibly extracts memories from a victim's soul, often causing severe spiritual damage or death.

old-fiend-fuhn.definition: A million-year-old Loose Immortal and a high-ranking elder of the Youngflame clan's Dongfu Commandery branch, known for his debauched lifestyle and fanatical loyalty.

fomenter-fulong.definition: A legendary Loose Immortal of the Shaoyin clan, known for his hedonistic lifestyle and long life of over a million years, making him a key node in the clan's defensive network.

ten-thousand-li-river.definition: A powerful magic treasure unleashed by Ji Ning that floods a vast region to destroy terrain and formation bases; used here to quickly create a breach in the enemy's defenses.

daoist-xuxiu.definition: A vile, unscrupulous disciple of Fomenter Fulong, known for procuring forbidden goods and slaves; his identity is used by Ji Ning to infiltrate the enemy lair.

spring-sun-hall.definition: The opulent, decadent main hall of Fomenter Fulong's palace, described as a 'kingdom of women,' highlighting his moral decay before his sudden and shocking death.

primordial-river-su.definition: The legendary river from Chinese mythology that flooded the earth during the time of the Great Yu. In Desolate Era, Ji Ning controls it as a devastating weapon and a tool of mercy.

seven-cycles-wind-and-thunder.definition: A powerful technique unleashed by Mu Northson’s Yixian puppet, producing a storm of wind and thunder that annihilates everything in its path.

vicious-old-fiend.definition: A million-year-old cultivator whose true body was just killed by Ji Ning; his second body survives to witness the coming storm.

five-celestial-immortals.definition: The five top-tier cultivators of the Shao'yan clan in this chapter: Huoba, Chixin, Jingyu, Kuumu, and Jinzhong.

lesser-yin-demon-sealing-formation.definition: A formation from the Primordial Fiendgod Era, designed to bind and capture powerful Fiendgods using five synergistic black chain treasures.

mountain-of-five-elements-defensive-form.displayTitle: Mountain of Five Elements Defensive Formation
surfaces: Mountain of Five Elements Defensive Formation
mountain-of-five-elements-defensive-form.definition: A common defensive formation in the Three Realms, where five cultivators merge their power to create a near-impenetrable five-colored mountain.

ten-thousand-li-suhe-river.definition: Ji Ning's acquired river-type magic treasure, used to entangle and slow enemies with its infinitely malleable water.

seven-wheels-wind-thunder.definition: A long-range attack technique or magical treasure that Mu Northson possesses.

lesser-yin-demon-subduing-formation.definition: A trapping formation from the Fiendgod Era, originally used to capture Fiendgods. It requires the capturer to be overwhelmingly stronger than the target to succeed.

endless-cupping-furnace.definition: An ancient artifact buried deep beneath the Shaoyin clan’s ancestral lands, described as an indestructible copper pillar embedded in a fiery red cliff. Its disturbance awakens a distant being.

starseizing-hand-fourth-revolution.definition: A divine ability that makes the cultivator’s hands comparable to Pure Yang supreme magic treasures, granting monstrous striking and pulling power.

pure-yang-supreme-magic-treasure.definition: The highest grade of magic treasure in the Three Realms hierarchy, far surpassing Immortal-ranked treasures in durability and power.
